text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper has found good support at $2,350 a tonne and may consolidate in its current range on Friday, but a close above $2,400 would give it a strong push, dealers said.
Aluminium might also continue to move sideways.
The Labour Party's landslide victory in U.K. elections could only have an indirect knock-on effect if stock prices fell.
COPPER - The market had found good support at $2,350 but a failure to extend gains might erode this buffer, analysts said on Friday.
"If it failed the $2,350 level again it could come back to $2,320 or $2,300," said one metals analyst in London. "It needs a good close above $2,410 for a continued upwards momentum," he added.
Although copper's fate looked shaky on the charts, analysts said continued labour unrest in Chile's mines could lead to a wave of short covering.
Martin Squires of brokers Rudolff Wolff said the prospect of significant disruption in production looked distant.
"(But) with copper stocks at uncomfortable levels, any disruption, however minor, could trigger further aggressive short covering," said Squires.
Workers at two of Chile's copper mines, Escondida and Quebrada Blanca, are on strike but disruption has been minor so far.
Technical indicators were flattening out, but a rise in LME stocks was likely to be short term as a result of the flare-up in the cash-threes backwardation last week, Squires said.
Traders said the market was unlikely to react to the Labour Party's landslide victory in the UK general election. But attention sharpened on stocks and currency markets.
"We have to see what the currencies and the stock market do. You may get a knock-on effect...but I can't see any reason why our election should upset the metals," said the London analyst.
Otherwise, trading conditions are likely to be quiet ahead of a three-day weekend in Britain.
Brokers Amalgamated Metal Trading said copper was in a band between $2,345 and $2,407 and could break either way.
By 0730 GMT three month copper was quoted at $2,360/$2,363 a tonne, a touch lower from Thursday's late close of $2,364/$2,368.
ALUMINIUM - Solid resistance at $1,650 must be cleared for a continued upward move, but the market was more likely to trend sideways, possibly garnering small gains, traders said.
Support was well establised at the $1,620-$1,615 region.
"If $1.622 fails to hold, falls to trendline support at $1,612 could be seen," said Amalgamated Metal in a daily review.

Brokers Brandeis said an appearance of a "bearish engulfing pattern" on the candlestick chart was disappointing, "However, the fact that the 10-day MA is rising up to cross the 30-day MA is positive."
At 0730 GMT three month aluminium was indicated at $1,627/$1,630 a tonne, barely changed from the late Thursday close of $1,628/$1,633.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
